metaDescription: Five Makita LXT cordless pole saws and couple-shaft kits compared on reach, bar length, brushless power and stand-alone versus multi-tool choices.
expertTake: The XAU02 telescoping 36V saw is the best Makita for owners who prune big trees, the XAU03Z articulating saw is the better choice for awkward angles and light branches, and the couple-shaft kits only make sense if you also want the string trimmer and hedge attachments. Anyone who does not already own Makita LXT batteries should price the batteries before the saw.
introParagraphs: This maker builds its cordless pole saws on a shared lithium battery platform, and several models use two batteries together for more power. That makes the saw tool only in many listings, because the batteries are the expensive part and are shared across its drills and mowers.
The real decision is between a dedicated pole saw and a power head with swappable attachments. They cost differently, store differently and reach differently, and that is where most buyers go wrong.

products.name: Makita XAU02PTB 36V Telescoping 10 Inch Pole Saw Kit
products.description:
The XAU02PTB is the kit version of Makita's best stand-alone pole saw. A brushless motor is claimed to deliver the power of a 30cc gas pole saw, and a telescoping shaft adjusts from 9 to 13 feet, so the same tool covers low limbs and high canopies. It runs on two 18V LXT batteries for a 36V system, and the kit includes 5.0Ah packs.

The maker quotes up to 140 cuts in 4x4 cedar with two 5.0Ah batteries, a number that depends on wood and chain condition. Treat it as a best case Treat it as a best case, but it signals real stamina for a cordless saw. In practice a homeowner trimming a yard of mature trees will work through a pair of batteries in a long afternoon, and having a second pair on the charger doubles that. The 10 inch bar is long enough for limbs of roughly 4 to 5 inches under the half-bar rule.

The kit costs more than the tool-only XAU02ZB, but includes batteries and a charger, which saves hunting for compatible packs. Oil the chain before each session, keep the bar clean and store the batteries cool. Check shaft locks for flex each season, since a wobbling telescoping pole is a safety issue. Wipe sap from the inner sections so they slide cleanly, and never extend the pole beyond its marked limit.
products.bestFor: Property owners with tall trees who want a complete, ready-to-use kit.
pros: Brushless motor in the 30cc gas class
Up to 140 cuts quoted with 5.0Ah packs

products.name: Makita XAU01ZB 36V 10 Inch Pole Saw, 8 Foot, Tool Only
products.description:
The XAU01ZB is the fixed-length sibling of the telescoping saw. It uses the same brushless motor and 10 inch bar, and Makita says it cuts 20 percent faster than a 31.4cc gas pole saw. The shaft is a rigid 8 feet, which removes the joints that can loosen on a telescoping pole.

A fixed shaft is stiffer and lighter, and a stiffer pole transmits less flex at the head, so cuts are steadier. The trade is reach: at 8 feet it works for lower limbs and fruit trees, but cannot match the 13 foot telescoping model for a tall canopy. Remember that your own height adds to the 8 feet, so a tall person standing on level ground can reach a limb at roughly 12 feet.

It is sold tool only, so you need two 18V LXT batteries and a dual charger. For an owner already holding LXT packs, it is a sensible purchase. If you are starting from nothing, add the cost of two batteries before you compare it with the kit. Oil and sharpen before each job. If you keep the batteries on a shelf with a dual charger, you can swap packs mid-job without losing the rhythm of the work.
products.bestFor: Lower limbs, fruit trees and owners who want a stiff, simple pole.
pros: Rigid shaft with no joints to loosen
20 percent faster than a 31.4cc gas unit, per Makita

products.name: Makita XAU03Z 18V 8 Inch Articulating Pole Saw, Tool Only
products.description:
The XAU03Z has a head that tilts through nine angle settings over a 120 degree range, which lets you cut branches from beside the trunk instead of directly below. That articulating head is the difference that matters in a crowded garden, because a straight pole forces you to stand under the limb.

It uses a single 18V battery, so it is lighter and cheaper to run than the 36V models, with an 8 inch bar and a split shaft that adjusts from 6 to 9 feet. The listing gives a total reach of up to 14 feet, a figure that includes your own reach. The smaller bar suits limbs up to about 3 to 4 inches. It is also easier to hold steady, since the shorter bar puts less leverage on your wrists.

An articulating head adds a pivot to maintain: keep the lock clean and tight, and check it before every session. Oil the chain and store the battery cool. Rinse resin from the head with a damp rag, and never submerge the tool.
products.bestFor: Awkward angles and light pruning on a single 18V battery.
pros: Articulating head with nine angle settings
cons: Pivot lock is another part to maintain

products.name: Makita XUX02SM1X4 Couple Shaft Kit, Trimmer and 10 Inch Saw
products.description:
This kit is a power head that accepts attachments rather than a dedicated pole saw. A brushless motor delivers up to 7,000 RPM on the 13 inch string trimmer attachment and a chain speed of 3,940 feet per minute on the 10 inch pole saw. Lever-style locks let you change attachments without tools.

The advantage is economy of storage and batteries: one head and one battery power several yard tools. That convenience is the whole case for the system. The disadvantage is that each attachment is a compromise, and a pole saw attachment is heavier at the end of the shaft than a dedicated saw. The 3,940 FPM chain speed equals about 65 feet per second, a competitive number.

It is the choice for someone who wants a trimmer and a pole saw but does not want to own two motors. Because the power head is the same one used on the trimmer, the battery runs down at the pace of whichever attachment is fitted, and a trimmer pulls less current than a chain. Keep couplings clean, grease the shaft joint as the manual directs and remove the battery when swapping. The chain on the attachment still needs bar oil, so keep a bottle with the kit.
products.bestFor: Owners who want one head for a trimmer and a pole saw.
pros: One power head runs several tools
No gas, oil mixing or pull starts
cons: Attachment saw is heavier at the end

products.name: Makita XUX02SM1X6 Couple Shaft Kit, Four Attachments

specList.label: Attachments
specList.value: String trimmer, pole saw, articulating hedge trimmer, blower

products.description:
The XUX02SM1X6 stretches the same idea across four attachments: a string trimmer, a pole saw, an articulating hedge trimmer and a blower. A high and low speed button helps manage power and run time, so you can drop to low for light work. Dropping to low extends runtime on a hedge, where you need little torque.

It is the most expensive Makita in the lineup, and you are paying for versatility. For a yard with trees, hedges, edges and paths, one kit replaces four tools and four motors, and every attachment uses the same battery.

A multi-tool is only worth it if you use all the attachments. Keep the couplings greased, store attachments in a dry place and check the locks before each use. The hedge and blower attachments share the same coupling, so a worn joint affects all four tools.
products.bestFor: Owners who want one battery system for four yard tasks.
cons: Pole saw attachment is not as light as a dedicated saw

buyingCriteria.explanation: The XAU01 and XAU02 use two 18V LXT batteries for 36V, while the XAU03Z and the couple-shaft kits use one. Two packs give more power and more weight at the head. That weight is what you feel after twenty minutes of overhead work. If you own only one 18V battery, the XAU03Z or a couple-shaft kit is the practical choice. Two 18V packs can also run other LXT tools.

The XAU02 telescopes from 9 to 13 feet, while the XAU01 is a rigid 8 feet. Telescoping joints add reach but must lock without flex, and a fixed shaft is stiffer. A telescoping pole also has more parts to clean after sap and dust get into the sections. Choose reach only if you need it. Most suburban limbs sit within 9 to 10 feet, so a fixed shaft often covers the job.

The 10 inch bars suit limbs of roughly 4 to 5 inches under the half-bar rule Chain speed also matters, since a fast chain on a long bar leaves a clean cut that heals better than a ragged one, and the 8 inch bar of the XAU03Z about 3 to 4. Always check Makita's stated maximum. Stand clear and cut large limbs in stages. Make an undercut first to prevent the bark from tearing down the trunk. A pole saw is for limbs, never trunks. Use a chainsaw for anything thicker.

The XAU03Z offers nine angle settings across a 120 degree range. It lets you cut from beside the limb, which is safer in a crowded garden. A straight pole suits open canopies. In a dense hedge line, the articulating head removes the need to lean awkwardly. The same head helps when you must cut under a branch from the side.

The couple-shaft kits power a trimmer and a pole saw from one head, trading specialisation for economy. A dedicated saw is lighter at the end of the pole. Decide how many yard tools you want to own. A single head also means one battery type and one charger.

The XAU02PTB includes 5.0Ah batteries, while the XAU01ZB is tool only. Batteries are the expensive part of the system. They also determine runtime more than the tool does. Price the whole set before comparing. A tool-only listing can look cheap until two batteries and a dual charger are added.

specDecoder.meaning: Two 18V LXT batteries working together. Power rises but so does head weight. Both packs must be charged and fitted before the tool will run.
specDecoder.watchFor: The XAU01 and XAU02 use two packs, the XAU03Z uses one.

specDecoder.meaning: Makita compares brushless torque to a 30cc gas saw. It is a marketing comparison, not a measurement. Do not buy on that claim alone. Compare chain speed and bar length instead.
specDecoder.watchFor: The XAU02 and XAU01 both claim 30cc gas power.

specDecoder.meaning: Cuts in 4x4 cedar with two 5.0Ah packs. Real counts depend on wood and chain. Green wood and dull chains reduce the count sharply.
specDecoder.watchFor: The XAU02 quotes up to 140 cuts.

specDecoder.meaning: Feet per minute at the chain. Divide by 60 for ft/s. That makes 3,940 FPM about 65 ft/s, which is fast for a cordless saw.
specDecoder.watchFor: The couple-shaft pole saw lists 3,940 FPM.

specDecoder.meaning: Maximum height including the operator. It is not the position of the saw tip.
specDecoder.watchFor: The XAU03Z lists up to 14 ft total.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and platform
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 36V two-battery saws with 18V single-battery saws and couple-shaft kits. The XAU02's brushless 36V system ranked highest for power. That ranking assumed a buyer who already accepts the cost of two batteries. Single-battery models earned weight credit. A lighter tool is easier to hold steady on a long reach. We looked at how the saw feels at full extension. A saw that feels fine at chest height can be tiring at full reach.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and geometry
howWeEvaluated.description: Shaft length, telescoping design and articulating heads were compared. The XAU02's 9 to 13 ft and the XAU03Z's nine angles earned credit. Short fixed poles lost reach points. A fixed pole is judged on stiffness instead.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling
howWeEvaluated.description: Head weight and balance decide fatigue. Two-battery saws carry more weight at the head. Single-battery models and fixed shafts did well. A heavy head at full reach is the fatigue factor.

howWeEvaluated.title: System value
howWeEvaluated.description: Couple-shaft kits spread a motor over several tools. We credited the XUX02SM1X6's four attachments but noted each is a compromise. Dedicated saws scored higher on cutting. Multi-tool kits scored higher on storage and cost per tool.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value tiering
howWeEvaluated.description: Relative price tiers ran from the XAU03Z up to the XUX02SM1X6. We weighed tiers against what is included, especially batteries. A kit with batteries is a better comparison than a bare tool.

cards.label: One 18V battery
cards.text: The XAU03Z and couple-shaft kits run on one pack, so they are lighter and cheaper to run.

cards.label: Two 18V batteries
cards.text: The XAU01 and XAU02 combine two packs into 36V for more cutting power, at the cost of head weight.

howToChoose.note: Pick one battery for light pruning and two for thick limbs. If in doubt, choose the lighter setup.

rows: One head for trimmer and saw

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A light head, a stiff pole and a short bar. Fruit limbs are small, so power matters less than balance.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The XAU01ZB's stiff 8 ft pole or the XAU03Z's articulating head suits fruit trees best.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You cut limbs over 3 inches or own a large property. The XAU02 is worth it.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You prune a few small branches. The XAU03Z on a single battery is enough.

maintenance.why: A dry chain dulls and overheats. Use bar oil. The oil reservoir on most saws holds enough for a few sessions, but check the level every time.
A dull chain binds and wastes battery. Keep the correct pitch. Many owners swap in a fresh chain and sharpen the old one later.
A loose telescoping lock or articulating pivot is unsafe. Clean and tighten. Check it with the battery removed, and replace any worn lock before it fails under load.
Lithium packs age in heat. Store partly charged. Keep them off a concrete floor in winter and out of a hot shed in summer.
Attachment couplings wear without grease. Clean before swapping. A dirty coupling can seat badly and wobble under load.

faq.q: Which Makita pole saw is best?
faq.a: The XAU02 is the best for tall trees, the XAU03Z for awkward angles and light pruning. The couple-shaft kits suit owners wanting multiple tools. If you only want a pole saw, choose a dedicated model.
Only for the XAU01 and XAU02, which run on 36V. Two packs mean two batteries to charge and store. The XAU03Z and couple-shaft kits run on one 18V pack.

faq.q: Is a multi-tool as good as a dedicated saw?
faq.a: No. A dedicated saw is lighter and cuts better. A multi-tool trades that for economy.
Treat it as marketing. It compares torque to a 30cc gas saw but is not a standard measurement. Real cutting speed also depends on chain sharpness.

faq.q: How thick a limb can I cut?
faq.a: About half the bar length, so around 4 to 5 inches on a 10 inch bar. Check the maker's maximum. Larger limbs need a chainsaw or an arborist.
Yes with care. Never cut a limb without deciding first where it will fall. Wear eye and head protection, stand outside the drop zone and never use it near power lines.
